description: Pikachu's debut in the Pokémon Trading Card Game, part of the 102-card Base Set that launched the TCG in the West. Early First Edition prints famously show Pikachu with red cheeks, later corrected to yellow — making the red-cheek variant one of the most sought-after error cards in the hobby.

The first ever Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles trading card set, released by Topps to ride the wave of the franchise's animated series and first feature film. It kicked off a run of TMNT card sets that continued into the 1990s.
estimatedValue: $5 – $50 for common cards, more for high-grade or rare inserts

setInfo: Vol.1, the first Official Card Game set (Japan)
description: Released February 4, 1999 in Japan, Vol.1 was the very first Yu-Gi-Oh! Official Card Game set, with 40 cards. Most cards were pulled from the manga and anime, but two — Fissure and Trap Hole — debuted here for the first time. Booster packs reportedly sold out everywhere at launch.
estimatedValue: Varies widely — rare Vol.1 cards can fetch hundreds to thousands of dollars

setInfo: Topps Nintendo Game Pack (with an earlier 1982 Topps Donkey Kong "Jumpman" card predating the Mario name)
description: Mario's trading card history is a bit tangled: his earliest card appearance is arguably the 1982 Topps Donkey Kong set, where he appears as "Jumpman" before the Mario name existed. The first card set to use the Mario/Nintendo branding directly was the 1989 Topps Nintendo Game Pack. A proper full "Super Mario Bros." set from Topps in the US never actually happened.

setInfo: Upper Deck Entertainment SpongeBob SquarePants Trading Card Game, Base Set
description: The first SpongeBob SquarePants trading card set, published by Upper Deck Entertainment on May 27, 2003 as a collectible card game tied to the show, four years after it first aired.
estimatedValue: $5 – $30, more for first-edition or holo variants
